semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Text-to-speech (TTS) is a specific type of speech synthesis, where the goal is to convert written text into spoken words. Hence, it is highly related and often considered the same in terms of application, focusing on generating spoken voice from text input.

parent_domains.justification: Speech processing is a broader domain that encompasses various aspects of handling and manipulating speech signals, including but not limited to synthesis. Speech synthesis is one of the tasks under speech processing.
Generative models for audio is a broader field that involves generating audio data, which includes speech synthesis as a specific application.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Speech processing is the closest parent because it directly pertains to processing speech, covering the synthesis, recognition, enhancement, and separation of speech. Speech synthesis is a fundamental task within the speech processing domain.

child_domains.justification: Text-to-speech is a specific instance of speech synthesis where the input is text data and the output is synthesized speech. It is a more constrained task under the speech synthesis domain.

closest_child_domain.justification: Text-to-speech is the closest child domain as it is directly and entirely a task of speech synthesis, focused specifically on converting text input into speech output.

sibling_domains.justification: Speech recognition shares the parent domain of speech processing with speech synthesis but focuses on converting spoken language into text, making it a sibling.
Speech enhancement is another task within speech processing that aims to improve the quality of speech signals, and is therefore a sibling to speech synthesis under the same parent domain.
Speech separation involves isolating individual speech signals from a mixture of sounds; like speech synthesis, it falls under the broader category of speech processing.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Speech recognition is the closest sibling as it involves similar methodologies and concerns related to how speech information is processed, albeit in reverse (i.e., from audio to text).

unrelated_domains.justification: Despite involving speech, this domain is more about translation between languages rather than the synthesis of speech.
This domain involves automatic generation of computer programs, unrelated to the audio domain.
This domain concerns the generation of video content, not related to speech.
This domain is about the automatic generation of code, unrelated to speech processing.
This field involves converting text descriptions into visual images, unrelated to any speech tasks.
While related to speech, this task focuses on identifying accents, which is more classification-focused rather than synthesis-focused.
This domain pertains to the synthesis of FPGA hardware descriptions, irrelevant to audio or speech.
Language modeling deals with predicting the next word in a sequence (mainly textual), which is different from synthesizing speech.
Although a generative process, this doesn't specify the context of speech or audio generation, making it less directly related.
Text generation is more about creating coherent and contextually relevant text content, separate from the speech synthesis domain.
This domain involves generating image content, which is unrelated to speech.
